name: Helium

discovery.discoverer: Pierre Janssen & Norman Lockyer (spectroscopically, in the Sun)

occurrence: Second most abundant element in the universe; on Earth it's trapped in natural gas deposits from radioactive alpha decay of heavier elements.
majorUses: Filling balloons and airships (non-flammable lift gas)
notableCharacteristics: Lowest boiling point of any element and the only substance that cannot be solidified by cooling alone at normal pressure — it needs extra pressure too.
ncertRelevance: why noble gases are chemically inert
whyHere: A completely filled 1s² shell gives it the stability every other atom is chasing — no unpaired electrons, no incentive to bond.
didYouKnow: Helium was discovered in the Sun's spectrum 27 years before it was found on Earth — its name comes from 'helios', Greek for sun.
genZNote: Found in the sun before it was found at home. Filled shell, filled ego, zero reactions.
